observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher is encouraging and conversational, explaining mechanics step-by-step with clear demonstrations. She breaks down the motion into smaller components and offers progressive practice tips like using a rubber band.

lesson_structure.note: Welcomes viewers and introduces learning fishtails.
Demonstrates initial backhand roll and catch.
Introduces the scoop with half-figure eight.
Emphasizes straight line pattern and common mistakes.
Shows self-help tip using a hair rubber band on the wrist.

steps_taught.name: Backhand roll
steps_taught.description: Roll the baton over the back of the hand to catch.

steps_taught.name: Fishtails
steps_taught.description: Scooping the baton back and forth in a straight line pattern.

what_works: Clear breakdown of hand positioning and motion direction
Useful prop hack with a rubber band for practice
what_hinders: Lack of structured counts or rhythm

quotes.text: The first thing you do is hold your baton so that it's lot-sided.
That's very important, not to cut your baton diagonally.
It just takes patience and a little bit of time.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher demonstrates holding the baton upright and moving the bottom part towards the shoulder into a backhand roll.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact finger pressure on the baton

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher scoops the baton to the front with a half figure-eight motion and rolls it back over the hand.

extraction.distinctive_method: Suggests using a hair rubber band around the wrist to help keep the baton in place while learning the fishtail motion.
